answer: In this PoA design, each identity is verified by a Wesolowski VDF: the prover must execute a fixed chain of sequential modular squarings, with every result depending on its predecessor, while a compact proof permits rapid verification. Cloning identities does not shorten any chain; GPUs may run chains separately but cannot parallelize one chain, imposing a strict physical time bottleneck. Thus echo, copper, and vine clones gain no instant quorum.
